name: IBL Finance Limited
sector: Non-deposit-taking Base-Layer NBFC; institutional and digital personal lending

quote.status: No 19 October print; ₹59.50 is the last observed 16 October close carried forward, predating the 19 October evening withdrawal announcement.

summary: IBL Finance is a small, predominantly institutional-lending NBFC with a legacy digital personal-loan book. The strongest support is reported FY26 equity of ₹61.10 crore against ₹57.85 crore borrowings; the decisive concern is asset realization and financeable growth, not negative industrial-style cash conversion. FY26 GNPA rose to 4.77%, wholesale NBFCs account for 60.58% of GNPA, and the top 20 borrowers represent 77.52% of advances. The ₹50 crore public NCD issue was withdrawn on 19 October 2026. At the carried-forward 16 October close ₹59.50, book valuation is 2.41 x and current-share earnings valuation 60.30 x despite 4.08% FY26 ROE. BQS, Growth Quality (GQS) and IAS are NS with explicit bounds, not invented low or neutral aggregates. G2/G3/G4 remain unresolved holds. No favorable new-purchase conclusion, ordinary return or entry price is supportable.
score_note: GQS means Growth Quality. All aggregates NS; no renormalization or invented midpoint.

BQS.bound_type: Mathematical missing-factor range, not a confidence interval; not rankable.

GQS.bound_type: Mathematical missing-factor range, not a confidence interval; not rankable.
overrides: If GQS becomes complete, CAP3 imposes maximum5.

IAS.bound_type: Mathematical missing-factor range, not a confidence interval; not rankable.

material_facts: Material related-party lending is disclosed and quantified.
Clean audit/CARO and reserve-transfer disclosures; no proved diversion in reviewed records.
GOV.contrary_fact_or_search: Related loans 8.10% of equity and director pay 16.96% PAT warrant scrutiny; clean opinion is not assurance of loan recovery.
GOV.rationale: Mixed stewardship evidence; no governance-failure override. Separate reliability hold addresses recovery evidence.

material_facts: No demonstrated proprietary loss-performance or captive-borrower advantage.
High-cost 11.5%–15.5% funding and concentrated FI borrowers constrain spread advantage.
MOAT.contrary_fact_or_search: Digital systems and established institutional relationships may lower process costs, but superior risk-adjusted returns have not been established.
MOAT.rationale: Contestable intermediary economics with weak observed excess returns; not penalized merely for small size.

material_facts: FY23–26 operating-revenue CAGR 8.8145% gives starting 4.
Two comparable FY26 half-years grew 38.68% and 27.00%, supporting one upward trajectory point.
REV.contrary_fact_or_search: Five-year CAGR 72.39% reflects an earlier product regime; June 26 growth slowed 10.85%.
REV.rationale: Preselected 3-year window around FI transition; +1 sustained two-half-year trajectory adjustment, final 5. No TAM/AUM bonus.

material_facts: Domestic FI/retail credit demand and loan-book expansion are real.
AUM 114.31 crore supports a measurable, not global-TAM, starting point.
DUR.contrary_fact_or_search: 77.52% top 20 exposure and withdrawn public funding restrict accessible runway.
DUR.rationale: Demand exists but financeable risk-controlled expansion remains unproved.

material_facts: Post-IPO FY25–26 ROE approximately 4.1% is well below 15%–20% cost-of-equity range.
FY24–26 incremental equity-return proxy 3.27%, with worsening GNPA.
CAP.contrary_fact_or_search: Large capital base provides loss absorption; gearing can raise ROE but also increases financing and credit risk.
CAP.rationale: Sector substitution: sustainable risk-adjusted ROA/ROE and capital retention, not industrial ROIC. Persistent sub-hurdle equity economics supports 3 and GQS cap 5.

material_facts: NPA stock and write-offs are verifiable and worsening.
Net loan accruals 4.3456 crore and deficient borrower-collateral recovery information remain material.
CASH.contrary_fact_or_search: Loan growth legitimately absorbs operating cash; negative CFO is not evidence of failed collections by itself.
CASH.rationale: NS pending vintage recoveries, accrual realization and borrower-security proof. No neutral score, no CFO/PAT scoring.

material_facts: Reported capital 49.36% and low book gearing offer a potential cushion.
Public NCD issue withdrawn; latest detailed contractual ALM is March, while funding is concentrated.
BAL.contrary_fact_or_search: No default evidenced in FY26 audit; historical ALM cumulative inflows exceed maturities under full recovery.
BAL.rationale: NS because current credible-stress liquidity, deposit availability and committed funding are not established; not automatically insolvency.

material_facts: Institutional loan-book expansion and listed equity fundraising were delivered.
Credit deterioration and unsuccessful public debt diversification show meaningful execution constraints.
EXEC.contrary_fact_or_search: Management withdrew the issue transparently and retains a low-geared book, so this is not proof of business failure.
EXEC.rationale: Observed outcomes mixed-to-weak; do not treat an industry forecast as a company promise.

material_facts: FY26 revenue rose 32.30% but PAT only 3.60%.
EPS remains below FY24; June 26 PAT fell despite revenue growth and minimal new loss expense.
EARN.contrary_fact_or_search: PAT remains positive and largely lending-derived; other income is small.
EARN.rationale: Weak risk-adjusted per-share translation, rather than one-off-driven profit inflation alleged without proof.

material_facts: Five-year annual lender model exposes required equity/funding.
Current undrawn commitments and post-withdrawal liquidity are not verified.
R.contrary_fact_or_search: Bull economic assumptions improve book value, but financeability is not established.
R.rationale: Ordinary and unfunded conditional returns remain null; return-spread schedule cannot be applied.

material_facts: Uncovered NPA exposure and concentrated borrowers can impair equity.
Bear assumptions breach capital buffers and need ongoing refinancing.
D.contrary_fact_or_search: Reported book capital provides some absorption, but collateral realization and current ALM are unresolved.
D.rationale: Cannot score supported survival/recovery using unverified current funding. Historical stress shown, not claimed current default.

material_facts: Price/book 2.4084 x with observed ROE 4.08% embeds a large improvement.
At 15% hurdle and 5% steady growth the reverse identity requires 29.08% ROE; even lower-cost peers do not establish that outcome for IBL.
P.contrary_fact_or_search: Early low leverage allows operational upside; changing loan mix might improve returns, but evidence is insufficient to assume it.
P.rationale: High expectations are independently visible in price versus current book earnings; no return inferred from an unfunded case.

material_facts: 60 full sessions contain 15 no-print days and median turnover ₹1.22 lakh.
At 5% volume participation no daily print supports one market lot.
L.contrary_fact_or_search: At 10%,5 lots fit the whole 60-session sample; trading is not proved permanently impossible.
L.rationale: Severely constrained lot-aware implementation at ₹5 lakh. L1 is not a missing-data substitute; full archive supports it.

gates.name: Integrity and minority protection
gates.reason: Related-party loans and remuneration warrant continuing checks, but no substantiated severe diversion or minority abuse identified.
gates.resolve: Independently substantiate related-party terms, approval and repayment.

gates.name: Financial reliability
gates.reason: Material borrower-book recoverability information is absent in Note 14, while a new wholesale NPA and a large net accrual/reversal balance need recovery evidence. A clean opinion does not cure this evidence gap. Normal cash-flow reclassifications, differing leverage definitions and rating-income definitions are reconciled, not treated as errors.
gates.resolve: Loan-level ageing/vintages, collateral/underlying-book verification, recovery evidence and accrual roll-forward reconcile with audited balances.

gates.name: Funding and survival
gates.reason: No current October stress ALM or verified available committed funding after withdrawn public NCD issue. Historical high capital and positive contractual gaps are not cash guarantees. No demonstrated actual default; Fail is not asserted.
gates.resolve: Current bank/deposit availability, secured-funding headroom, liabilities and realistic collection stress independently support operations without rescue.

gates.name: Tradability
gates.reason: Full 60-session archive supports L1;2,000-share lots make 5% participation infeasible on every observed session. No post-withdrawal trade or live depth verified. Not declared suspended.
gates.resolve: Post-news two-sided executable depth and a lot-aware entry/exit plan at the actual position.

reconciliations.explanation: FY25 comparator moved loan advances and other asset investment from investing into operating. Total cash change unchanged. This is legitimate lender classification, not a reliability charge.
FY26 comparative reallocates approximately ₹2.75 lakh between operating liabilities and financing. Closing cash unchanged; immaterial presentation change, not misconduct.

RHP Annexure V reconciles additional expenses. FY21–22 use restated history; FY23 display latest annual comparator and retain the separate restated figure. Growth of revenue is unaffected; cross-basis profit CAGR is not used. RHP cash-flow table mixes original PBT and financing costs, so old CFO is descriptive only.
Different numerator scope, not contradiction; true regulatory denominator is owned fund after prescribed deductions.
Rating expressly uses net interest income plus other income; do not compare it to gross operating revenue or allege a discrepancy.

model_policy_notes.capital_limit: This is an analytical haircut, not the issuer regulatory NOF calculation. The unidentified other-assets balance is not asserted to be prepaid expense. Exact subsidiary/group-exposure and other statutory deductions are unverified.
model_policy_notes.required_liquidity: Three crore of existing term deposits are preserved as unavailable-to-growth plus max(0.681 crore,2% gross loans) operating liquidity. This is a conservative assumption, not a finding that all deposits are legally restricted.
model_policy_notes.preserved_other_net_assets: Other net assets remain at2.6663 crore including accruals and advances; no cash release or incremental value is added. Realizability is unresolved and ordinary valuation outputs remain null.
model_policy_notes.funding: Debt-rollover and growth cash requirements are signed and unverified, never filled from proposed issuance; first bridge is assumed, not observed October balances.

annual_models.forecast_anchor: Audited 31 March 2026, with explicit assumed bridge to 19 October. June P&L provides a cross-check, not a fabricated June balance sheet.

evidence.claim: Exact ISIN INE0O7401018 is IBL Finance Limited / IBLFL on NSE Emerge, not IBL Group or IIFL. Incorporated 2017; RBI Co R B.01.00589, non-deposit-taking Base-Layer NBFC. No subsidiaries, JVs or associates. Indian GAAP/AS, not Ind AS.
evidence.scope: Standalone IBL Finance unless explicitly stated
evidence.limitation: RBI registration is reported in primary issuer documents and audited CARO; independent current certificate-status registry was not retrieved.

evidence.claim: FY26 operating revenue 17.1428 crore, PAT 2.4403, equity 61.0963; FY25 revenue 12.9572, PAT 2.3554, equity 58.656.
evidence.scope: Standalone IBL Finance unless explicitly stated
evidence.limitation: Material uncertainty concerns loan recoverability and cash availability, not transcription of these reported totals.

evidence.claim: FY23–26 revenue CAGR 8.8145%; FY21–26 CAGR 72.3917%; the earlier window includes pandemic-era microloan/digital scaling and predates the FI-lending pivot.
evidence.scope: Standalone IBL Finance unless explicitly stated
evidence.limitation: No acquisitions found, but product/yield mix changed materially. Loan-book or disbursement CAGR is not a substitute for revenue.

evidence.claim: Gross NPA 2.5657→5.4509 crore and ratio 2.54%→4.77%; net NPA 1.99%→3.69%; current June ratios 4.81%/3.72%. FY26 GNPA additions 5.0136 less reductions 2.1284 reconcile closing balance.
evidence.scope: Standalone IBL Finance unless explicitly stated
evidence.limitation: Vintage loss curves, cures versus recoveries within reductions and current collection efficiency are ND.

evidence.claim: FY26 loss expense 1.9848 crore includes 1.2294 write-offs, 0.7137 NPA provision and 0.0417 standard provision. NPA reserve 1.2782 implies 23.45% coverage; wholesale NBFCs account for 60.58% of GNPA.
evidence.scope: Standalone IBL Finance unless explicitly stated
evidence.limitation: RBI minimum provisioning is not evidence of economic loss sufficiency. Short write-off policy can reduce reported delinquency stock.

evidence.claim: Note 14 assumes recovery despite unavailable underlying borrower-book recoverability details. Net accrued loan amounts 4.3456 crore include 12.2120 crore reversal against 16.5576 gross accruals.
evidence.scope: Standalone IBL Finance unless explicitly stated
evidence.limitation: Need borrower collateral realization and accrual-vintage reconciliation; no assertion that disclosed amounts are false.

evidence.claim: FY26 top 20 borrowers 88.6079 crore, 77.52% of advances; June four funding counterparties 47.2919 crore, 68.89% of outside liabilities, and top 10 borrowings 97.67%.
evidence.scope: Standalone IBL Finance unless explicitly stated
evidence.limitation: Geographic/end-use mix is not direct borrower diversification. A loan secured by another lender’s book retains underlying unsecured consumer/MSME exposure.

evidence.claim: Acuité March 2026 BBB−/Stable assessed no FI delinquency through September 2025 and well-matched ALM then; later FY26 wholesale NPAs are genuine deterioration, not a contradiction at identical dates.
evidence.scope: Standalone IBL Finance unless explicitly stated
evidence.limitation: Rated proposed limits 50+50 crore are neither debt already outstanding nor committed available cash.

evidence.claim: 19 October 2026 board withdrew ongoing public NCD issue; management cited banking/UPI/ASBA problems and inadequate expected minimum subscription, and asserted stability would be unaffected.
evidence.scope: Standalone IBL Finance unless explicitly stated
evidence.limitation: The withdrawal is verified; causal explanations and future stability are management statements. No 50-crore proceeds assumed.

evidence.claim: FY26 debt 57.8485 crore, cash headline 3.681, but 3.0 in fixed deposits; readily liquid cash/bank/wallet only 0.681. Current principal maturities in note 5 plus overdraft are material despite a high headline current ratio.
evidence.scope: Standalone IBL Finance unless explicitly stated
evidence.limitation: Deposit encumbrances and current withdrawal access unverified. Contractual loan maturities are not guaranteed collections.

evidence.claim: Related-party loans 4.95 crore, 4.33% of exposure and 8.10% of equity; director remuneration 0.4139 crore or 16.96% of PAT. Technology services include related Codexial.
evidence.scope: Standalone IBL Finance unless explicitly stated
evidence.limitation: Arm’s-length status is management/audit disclosure, not independent price verification; no substantiated diversion found.

evidence.claim: FY26 ROE 4.0756% and ROA 2.0106%; FY24–26 incremental equity-return proxy 3.2696%. IPO capital raised existing equity substantially but EPS 1.17 FY24→0.95 FY25→0.99 FY26.
evidence.scope: Standalone IBL Finance unless explicitly stated
evidence.limitation: Sector CAP uses risk-adjusted equity returns, not nonfinancial ROIC. Two-year post-IPO proxy not project IRR; three/five-year proxies distorted by changing capital/mix.

evidence.claim: June 26 special-purpose quarter revenue 4.5031 crore(+10.85%), PAT 0.3512(−8.18%); credit loss expense only 0.0186 versus 0.8385 prior quarter while NPA stock remains elevated.
evidence.scope: Standalone IBL Finance unless explicitly stated
evidence.limitation: Comparator not limited-reviewed. A single quarter is not annualized, and loss timing requires explanation.

evidence.claim: As of 19 October no trade print; latest 16 October close 59.50.24,730,650 issued shares imply 147.1474 crore market cap, 2.4084 x FY26 book and 60.2989 x FY26 current-share earnings.
evidence.scope: Standalone IBL Finance unless explicitly stated
evidence.limitation: Stale quote predates the withdrawal news; not executable or evidence of price discovery after it.

evidence.claim: 60 sessions:15 zero-print days, mean turnover ₹321343.33, median ₹122000. At 5% participation no session accommodates one 2,000-share lot;4-lot ₹476000 position requires higher impact or unavailable capacity.
evidence.scope: Standalone IBL Finance unless explicitly stated
evidence.limitation: Historical print volume is not live order-book depth. No finite whole-lot 5% exit estimate; continuous proxy 78.03 days understates discreteness.

evidence.claim: Borrowing coupons 11.5%–15.5% and first/exclusive borrower-book security do not establish a structural moat; operating revenue growth increasingly depends on funding and loan-loss discipline.
evidence.scope: Standalone IBL Finance unless explicitly stated
evidence.limitation: Digital processing/underwriting claims are management assertions without disclosed mature cohort loss superiority.

evidence.claim: RBI Base-Layer leverage maximum 7 uses total outside liabilities divided by owned funds; reported 0.95 debt/equity and 1.13 outside-liability/book-equity are different scopes.
evidence.scope: Standalone IBL Finance unless explicitly stated
evidence.limitation: Modeled owned-fund deductions and 20%-loan equity buffer are conservative analytical proxies, not a certification of regulatory capital.

evidence.claim: FY24 loan cash-outflow reclassification 17.1159 crore explains CFO−13.3986→−30.5145 and investing−18.6941→−1.5782 with no cash change. FY25 later comparative moves 0.0275 between CFO/CFF.
evidence.scope: Standalone IBL Finance unless explicitly stated
evidence.limitation: Normal lender classification/presentation differences are not an allegation or a CFO/PAT penalty.

evidence.claim: In a steady residual-income identity, 2.4084 x book with 15% required equity return and 5% perpetual growth requires approximately 29.08% sustainable ROE, versus 4.08% observed.
evidence.scope: Standalone IBL Finance unless explicitly stated
evidence.limitation: Steady-state diagnostic, not a price target or full intrinsic value; growth below discount rate. Lower terminal multiples make five-year economics harder.

evidence.claim: Northern Arc management reported Q3FY26 cost of funds 8.5%, ROE 10.7%, GNPA 1.36%/NNPA 0.69%; UGRO FY26 issuer release reports 2.5%/1.6%, ROA 2.1%, with acquired Profectus included.
evidence.scope: Standalone IBL Finance unless explicitly stated

sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text: IBL Finance is a small, predominantly institutional-lending NBFC with a legacy digital personal-loan book. The strongest support is reported FY26 equity of ₹61.10 crore against ₹57.85 crore borrowings; the decisive concern is asset realization and financeable growth, not negative industrial-style cash conversion. FY26 GNPA rose to 4.77%, wholesale NBFCs account for 60.58% of GNPA, and the top 20 borrowers represent 77.52% of advances. The ₹50 crore public NCD issue was withdrawn on 19 October 2026. At the carried-forward 16 October close ₹59.50, book valuation is 2.41 x and current-share earnings valuation 60.30 x despite 4.08% FY26 ROE. BQS, Growth Quality (GQS) and IAS are NS with explicit bounds, not invented low or neutral aggregates. G2/G3/G4 remain unresolved holds. No favorable new-purchase conclusion, ordinary return or entry price is supportable. This is an unproven lender-scaling thesis, not an established compounder, and a cheaper quote alone would not resolve underwriting, liquidity or lot-size constraints. Reconsider only after current funding and borrower recoverability evidence support risk-adjusted per-share compounding.

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text: Cutoff 20 October 2026,23:59 IST; information dated after cutoff excluded from the conclusion even though retrieved 21 October. Exact issuer IBL Finance Limited, INE0O7401018, IBLFL, NSE Emerge. Standalone Indian-GAAP/AS accounts, no subsidiaries/JVs/associates. Five-year horizon 19 October 2026–19 October 2031,15% nominal annual equity hurdle before investor taxes; cost of equity independently assumed 15%–20%,17% for residual income. ₹5 lakh is only a research reference, not an allocation recommendation. No 19 October print exists: ₹59.50 is 16 October close, before withdrawal news. Market cap ₹147.1474 crore. Confidence: High on primary reported totals and historical liquidity; Medium on product-adjusted growth and governance; Low on asset recovery, current funding and executable valuation. Overall conclusion confidence is Low, governed by material unresolved subjects. Gates are detailed separately, with G1 Conditional and G2/G3/G4 Hold.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text: All 13 factor audits and exact Decimal contributions are embedded. BQS known sum 3.38, coverage 82%, missing-data bound 3.56–5.18; GQS known sum 4.05, coverage 90%, raw bound 4.15–5.05 and maximum 5 if completed because CAP3; IAS known sum 0.30, coverage 20%, bound 1.10–8.30. All three final aggregates remain NS, with no redistributed weights, midpoint or cap substituted for an incomplete score. GOV5, MOAT3, REV5, DUR5, CAP3, EXEC4, EARN4, P2, L1; CASH, BAL, R, D remain NS. Moving the two uncertain scored factors GOV and MOAT ±1 moves BQS known sum by±0.40, not enough to remove the evidence hold. GQS means Growth Quality. No ranking is allowed while material reliability is unresolved.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text: IBL lends principal and earns interest plus processing charges, rather than operating a fee-only fintech platform. Personal loans are marketed up to ₹50,000 for up to 12 months; FI loans up to ₹5 crore for up to 24 months. Acuité described 90% FI exposure at September 2025. FY26 interest income ₹15.5505 crore and loan fees ₹1.5923 crore reconcile operating revenue ₹17.1428 crore. Borrower lenders on-lend into personal loans, MSME, MFI, LAP, vehicles and gold. The FY26 end-use personal-loan share 53% is look-through exposure, not proof that 53% is directly originated personal lending. Direct borrower concentration therefore matters more than a diversified end-use chart. Non-deposit-taking Base-Layer status means no public deposit franchise; an NCD is funding, not revenue.

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text: Mechanism proposed: proprietary digital underwriting→fast onboarding and repeat borrowers→lower origination cost. Evidence: proprietary apps and operational deployment are disclosed, but cohort loss superiority, retention pricing, market share and through-cycle funding advantage are not established. Failure mode: larger lenders match distribution while IBL borrows at 11.5%–15.5%, or borrowers suffer correlated underlying unsecured losses. Northern Arc provides a stronger funding/scale comparator, but its Q3FY26 management metrics are dated and mixed retail/intermediated business; UGRO provides a risk/distribution comparator with FY26 acquisition-influenced consolidated figures. Arman is a weaker-cycle microfinance comparator, but its FY26 underlying presentation could not be retrieved, so no snippet numbers enter valuation. No peer multiple is mechanically transferred. A security interest in an NBFC loan book is not the same as readily realizable hard collateral.

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text: FY21–26 operating revenue is ₹1.1259, 3.2708, 13.3052, 14.1224, 12.9572, 17.1428 crore. Five-year CAGR 72.39% is reported for completeness, but includes pandemic-era/digital microloan scaling before the FY24 FI pivot;10-year CAGR is ND, not zero. Preselected three-year current-regime window FY 23–26 gives 8.81%, starting REV4. FY26 half-years ₹8.1551 and ₹8.9877 crore versus ₹5.8806 and ₹7.0766 grew 38.68% and 27.00%; this supports at most+1 trajectory point. June 26 grew 10.85%, so it does not justify another adjustment. FY26 interest rose ₹4.1829 crore while fees rose only ₹0.0027 crore: nearly all incremental operating revenue came from interest/mix/book deployment, not fee proliferation. TTM to June 26 is FY 26+Q1FY27−Q1FY26=₹17.5835 crore revenue and ₹2.4090 crore PAT; prior quarter not limited-reviewed. No single quarter is annualized.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text: Gross loans increased ₹50.7550→100.9924→114.3111 crore in FY 24–26, but this growth is not revenue and is not automatically value creation. FY26 retained earnings add ₹2.4403 crore against incremental gross loans ₹13.3187 crore; other funding and repayments must be reconciled. CAP uses risk-adjusted ROA/ROE, loss vintages and retained regulatory capital, not industrial incremental ROIC. FY26 ROE 4.08% is far below an explicit 15%–20% equity cost range; a two-year post-IPO incremental equity-return proxy is 3.27%. Longer proxies are distorted by IPO and product shifts, so they are not project IRRs. The linked model tests−5%,10%,20% annual loan growth with yields, expenses, losses, capital retention and refinancing. Every projected borrowing request remains unverified, the withdrawn issue contributes zero, and no funded-growth conclusion follows from a large accessible credit market.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text: Promoters held about 63.20% at March 2026; later September aggregator percentage is not substituted for an independently reviewed primary filing. Related-party loans ₹4.95 crore are 4.33% of advances and 8.10% of equity; they are unsecured in the long-term loan note, with disclosed interest and no reported NPA. Director remuneration ₹0.4139 crore is 16.96% of PAT. Related technology/professional-service transactions are quantified, not assumed abusive. Auditor H R M & Co. issued an unmodified FY26 opinion, reported an operational audit trail and no borrowing default. No separate guarantee, contingent liability or capital commitment is reported in note 33; no hidden guarantee is assumed zero outside reviewed scope. Observable delivery: January 2024 IPO funds expanded equity; FY24–26 FI scaling delivered book growth; March 2026 rating broadened a funding route; October 2026 public NCD fundraising was withdrawn. Company explanations for the withdrawal remain attributed, not independently endorsed. Prior bonus issues change units, not economic ownership; FY24 fresh IPO shares are real dilution, current issued shares 24,730, 650.

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text: Full six-year histories, interim data and source reconciliations are embedded. FY26 PAT ₹2.4403 crore versus FY 25₹2.3554 grew 3.60% on 32.30% revenue growth; finance cost ₹6.1847 nearly doubled, loss expense ₹1.9848 rose 49.71%, and net margins compressed. PAT+depreciation is not distributable lender cash. CFO−₹3.4027 crore, investing−₹0.5423 and financing ₹4.7986 reconcile cash growth ₹0.8536; interest is in financing, so an after-interest operating cash view is−₹9.5874 before capex, still not a quality ratio. Loan-book deployment legitimately consumes cash. FY24₹17.1159 crore loan reclassification and FY25₹0.0275 crore presentation change are reconciled without alleging manipulation. Gross loan assets ₹114.3111 plus net accrued loan amounts ₹4.3456 reconcile financing advances ₹118.6567. Net accrual reversal, rapidly rising wholesale GNPA and Note 14 missing recovery details require borrower-level proof. FY26 NPA additions ₹5.0136 are 4.96% of opening loans; total credit cost 1.84% of average loans and write-offs are analyzed separately. Headline cash ₹3.681 includes ₹3.0 fixed deposits, not assumed immediately available. Advance-to-service-provider ₹2.0154, tax assets and prepayments are not freely distributable cash and are not added to equity value. Current maturities embedded in long-term borrowing notes defeat a naive current-ratio inference.

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text: Use retained-equity/book-value evolution and annual residual income, with P/B and P/E cross-checks. Operating debt is already part of lender equity economics; do not compute industrial EV/EBITDA or subtract debt again from book-equity value. At ₹59.50, P/B 2.4084 x and FY26 current-share P/E 60.2989 x. The steady-state identity P/B=(ROE−g)/(ke−g) implies 29.08% sustainable ROE forke 15% andg 5%, versus 4.08% observed; sensitivities useke 12/15/18% andg 0/5/7%. Annual models include explicit 31 March–19 October 2026 forecast bridge, then exact five-year dated stubs/full fiscal years through 19 October 2031. All ordinary returns, entry prices, residual-income valuation points and unfunded conditional returns are null. Mechanical terminal prices are not targets: they only show what assumed books/multiples imply before feasibility. Borrowing repayment and gross refinancing requests are explicit, not net funding confused with cumulative debt. Minimum NOF follows the existing-ICC ₹5 crore to ₹10 crore glide path by 31 March 2027; the deduction and 20%-loan buffer tests are analytical proxies, not verified regulatory certification. The model assumes all forecast interest and fees are collected; this unverified realization assumption is one reason no executable case is released. All deposits/operating buffers stay in the equity ledger; dividends are zero, cash is not added twice, and a separate first-bridge rescue illustrates 5% issuance fees and dilution without assuming rescue exists.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text: Main falsification variable: recovery-adjusted lending spread, not reported disbursal growth. Correlated FI borrower stress→underlying unsecured collections deteriorate→IBL collateral realization disappoints→credit loss and suspended interest rise→funding reprices or matures without renewal→growth stops and equity dilution/forced asset sales follow. Low initial gearing is the strongest contrary evidence and can absorb losses, but does not create immediate cash or prove each collateral pool. FY26 PCR 23.45% leaves a substantial gross NPA balance unprovided; recovery estimates therefore matter. Historical March contractual ALM is cash-tested at 100/50/25% principal realization, preserving deposits and ignoring noncash assets as liquidity. Its source row labeled B−A actually displays A−B signs; arithmetic is explicitly corrected, not represented as a new cash source. This is not a current October stress forecast. Impairment risk is High; a hypothetical bear can breach capital buffers, but current actual insolvency/default is not established.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: No supported multibagger thesis is established. Without distributions,5× in five years requires 37.97% annual per-share appreciation and 10× requires 58.49%. Holding terminal P/B at 1 x and no dilution would require book value per share to reach ₹297.50 or ₹595.00 from ₹24.7047, roughly 12.04× or 24.08× book growth, far beyond present 4.08% ROE retention. A higher terminal multiple simply moves the burden onto valuation persistence; funding, credit costs and dilution still constrain book growth. Classification: Speculative / unsupported, not a quantified probability. The model never turns gross loan growth into a stock-return forecast without required funding.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text: Eight company-specific checkpoints:1) GNPA/NNPA versus June 4.81/3.72%; investigate any continued rise and require loan-level resolution of wholesale defaults.2) Credit charge/write-offs versus FY 26₹1.9848/₹1.2294 crore and June ₹0.0186 charge; reconcile timing, not demand artificially stable ratios.3) Top 20 borrower concentration 77.52%; concentration above this without better risk coverage weakens diversification.4) Net loan accruals ₹4.3456 and reversal ₹12.2120; any growth without cash/vintage reconciliation maintains G 2.5) Current available cash versus historical ₹0.681 liquid and debt maturities; negative stressed cumulative cash without committed funds is a thesis break.6) Replacement funding after withdrawn issue; approval or rating alone is insufficient.7) Risk-adjusted ROE versus 4.08% and hurdle 15%; require sustained per-share progress, not just levered AUM growth.8) Live lot-aware liquidity and post-news trades;5%-participation capacity must improve before an implementation case. Review at next filed half-year, borrowing update and material credit event. These are research conditions, not an automatic monitoring subscription.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text: Hold — unresolved; not eligible for quality, growth-quality or investment rankings. Governance G 1 is Conditional rather than Fail; financial reliability G 2, funding G 3 and tradability G 4 remain unresolved. BQS/GQS/IAS are all NS with exact mathematical bounds. CAP3 sets a GQS maximum 5 only if remaining evidence becomes scoreable; it does not replace NS. A clean audit, substantial equity and real revenue growth support continued investigation, while deteriorating asset quality, expensive funding, premium book valuation and market-lot constraints prevent a favorable new-position conclusion. A lower quote alone is insufficient: recoverability, accrual realization, present liquidity/commitments and executable depth must first be established. No ordinary expected return or buy-under number is released.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text: Source register contains underlying annual reports, IPO and NCD prospectuses, a special-purpose June quarter, liquidity disclosure, rating rationale, the exact 19 October withdrawal filing and dated NSE archives/master. Pages and hashes identify the reviewed copies; hashes are integrity fingerprints, not independent authentication or verification that reported transactions occurred. Search/landing pages do not substitute for underlying documents. Arman retrieval failed; UGRO underlying PDF was read through web extraction but could not be byte-downloaded. No raw issuer PDF/OCR/image/shareholder-ID material is included in the private research packages. Open questions: current ALM, available funding and collateral headroom; loan vintages/recoveries and related-party repayment; service-provider advances and accrual-reversal bridge; capital deductions and protected liquidity; current promoter pledge/encumbrance record and post-news executable depth. Scenarios are analyst assumptions, not company guidance. Values omitted because missing are null/ND/NS, never zero.
